scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on the CS LAB 1 PC (192.168.2.3) reports they cannot reach
the Server Room (1.0.0.x) or the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x). The
IT Department PCs are also affected. Other zones (Office, Principle,
Internet Lab itself) can still reach each other. What's wrong?
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router0 ripd daemon
Mechanism: router0 is the only L3 hop between IT Dept
  (192.168.1.0/24), CS Dept (192.168.2.0/24), and the rest
  of the network (reached via Serial2/0 to router1). When
  ripd dies on router0, router1 ages out the 192.168.1.0/24
  and 192.168.2.0/24 prefixes, and router0 itself stops
  learning the 1.0.0.0/8 / 128.168.0.0/16 / 192.168.3.0/24
  / 192.168.4.0/24 prefixes from router1. IT + CS PCs become
  isolated from everything beyond router0.
Localization: router0
Root cause: RIP routing daemon (ripd) not running on router0
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration on router0 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ripd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router rip` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ripd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the rip configuration is missing/empty on router0" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ripd daemon on router0 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
router0). Once ripd is running again it re-learns the remote prefixes and
re-advertises 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, restoring IT Dept and CS Dept
reachability.

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ripd back CONFIG-LESS and the rip service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ripd AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration (network statements) on router0. A proposal that restores the missing rip configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Dynamic routing on router0 (FRR/RIP) is not running/configured, so router0 only knows its directly connected subnets.

Mechanism: From CS Lab (192.168.2.0/24) and IT Dept (192.168.1.0/24), traffic must traverse router0 -> router1 -> router2 to reach Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16). Because router0 has no routes to those remote networks, it immediately returns ICMP “Destination Net Unreachable” to the hosts, breaking reachability. Other zones (Office 192.168.3.0/24 and Principle 192.168.4.0/24 on router1, and Internet Lab/Server Room on router2) still interconnect because RIP is up between router1 and router2.

Localization: The failures originate on router0 interfaces serving CS and IT (eth1 192.168.2.1 and eth0 192.168.1.1). Evidence:
- Pings from cs_lab1 to 1.0.0.5 and 128.168.0.2 return “From 192.168.2.1 Destination Net Unreachable.”
- Pings from it_lab1 to 128.168.0.2 return “From 192.168.1.1 Destination Net Unreachable.”
- router0 has only connected routes; FRR is inactive (systemctl: “Active: inactive (dead)”), and vtysh shows no RIP config.
- router1/router2 have RIP configured and show learned routes to 1.0.0.0/8, 128.168.0.0/16, and 192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24 via RIP.

Root cause: FRR (RIP) is disabled/missing configuration on router0, so it neither advertises 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24 nor learns routes to 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16.

Corrective fix: Enable and configure RIP on router0, then start FRR:
- In FRR: router rip; network 192.168.1.0/24; network 192.168.2.0/24; network 10.0.0.0/8; version 2.
- systemctl enable --now frr.
Alternatively, add static routes on router0 to 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 via 10.10.0.2.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names router0 as the affected device (dynamic routing/FRR/RIP on router0).
The report explicitly identifies FRR/RIP on router0 as not running/configured (noting FRR inactive and missing RIP config), which corresponds to the ripd/RIP component failure.
The report explicitly states IT and CS hosts are isolated while other zones (office, principle, server room, internet) remain reachable, matching the expected symptom cluster.
Recommends re-enabling/configuring RIP on router0 and starting FRR (and gives a valid static-route alternative), which matches the expected remediation.

The log contains direct evidence: frr is inactive on router0, ripd.conf is empty, vtysh running-config on router0 has no 'router rip', and pings show ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' from router0 addresses — supporting the diagnosis that RIP is not running/configured on router0 and causes isolation. One minor unsupported assertion in the writeup (that router1/router2 show learned routes to 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24) is not shown in the log.
